answer: Bind each identity to a long-standing social-security contribution record: the platform stores only a hash of a record showing several years of regular contributions, verified through the issuing authority, and rejects any second identity presenting the same hash. A sybil farmer would need years of real contributions per fake account, turning cheap duplication into a slow, expensive river of paperwork that cannot be rushed. It is not velvet-smooth for everyone: workers outside formal employment would be excluded, and the scheme still trusts the issuer not to leak the underlying umber files.
